text:
maria: Heads up — saw a new flake pattern on us-east gpu nodes: thermal spike -> burst of Xid=31/25 errors -> kube drains the whole node and we lose 8 GPUs at once. Happened 3x in the past 24h.
ajay: ugh. Is this the soft-drain automation triggering on aggregate node-level Xid counts?
maria: yes, current rule: if node_xid_rate > 5/m for 2m -> cordon & drain. Works but too coarse.
carlos: Can we fence at the GPU level? taint only the impacted GPU so other GPUs stay schedulable? our device-plugin supports per-GPU allocation metadata.
priya: We already have per-gpu metrics from node-exporter + nvidia-smi exporter. The issue is kube drain is per-node; slurm does per-partition. Need a unified flow.
laura: Proposal draft: "soft-cordon-per-gpu" heuristic: 1) track Xid spikes per GPU id (ring buffer 1m/5m), 2) if a single GPU hits threshold -> mark DeviceUnavailable for that GPU in the device-plugin and apply a node-level annotation so autoscaler knows capacity decreased by 1, 3) only evict pods that have guaranteed allocation on that GPU (GPU-exclusive pods), leave multi-gpu pods untouched until >N gpus affected.
ajay: love it. Add hysteresis: require recovery (no XIDs) for 10m before unmarking. Also cap simultaneous GPU fencing to avoid cascading reschedules during region-wide heat event.
maria: Agree. Also want fallback: if >50% GPUs on node are marked within 5m -> escalate to full node drain with higher priority to avoid corrupt states.
infra-bot: [alert] 2013-09-01T12:03:00Z node/gpu-us-east-42 reported XID burst (gpu0: 12 in 60s)
carlos: For slurm we can add a prolog/epilog that queries the device-plugin annotation and requeues jobs pinned to the fenced GPU, but we need to avoid job churn for short spikes. Suggest requeue window of 2m and a max retries param.
priya: Ops checklist for rollout: - unit tests for device-plugin annotation read/write - prometheus rule: per-gpu XID rate - e2e using synthetic XID injector on staging - capacity impact simulation (scale down/up)
laura: Metrics to watch post-rollout: fenced_gpu_count, requeues_due_to_fence, node_full_drains_triggered, scheduling_delay_p95 for gpu pods, cost_delta_jvm (monthly).
ajay: Implementation notes: prefer agent-side enforcement (on-node daemon) to beat kubelet race; comms via K8s API server annotations + CRD optional. Keep policy configurable per-cluster (prod stricter than non-prod).
maria: Security/observability: every fence action should emit an audit log + trace id and link to the incident in console. Add a temporary /debug endpoint to un-fence if we need manual override.
carlos: One risk: short-lived training jobs with checkpointing — we should prefer graceful migrate vs kill. Add policy: if job has checkpoints and remaining walltime > 15m -> attempt to migrate, else kill and requeue.
priya: Can someone sketch a prometheus alert rule for the per-gpu XID? I can wire it to notify infra-bot.
laura: example rule: 
```
- alert: PerGPUXidBurst
  expr: increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_count{job="node-exporter"}[1m]) > 8
  for: 30s
  labels: { severity: warning }
  annotations: { runbook: "/runbooks/gpu-xid-burst.md" }
```
maria: Nice. Let's also add a rate-limiter so we don't fence/unfence repeatedly: min-seconds-between-actions = 120.
ajay: Test plan: - canary cluster with 50 nodes - enable soft-cordon-per-gpu with conservative thresholds - run synthetic heat + xid injector - measure false positives < 1% - rollback if node_full_drains > baseline + 2
maria: I'll draft the RFC and link to the pr. Assigning owners: infra:ajay, device-plugin:carlos, sre:priya, rollout:laura.
priya: I'll spin up a staging job to simulate mixed batch + gpus and share logs.
carlos: I'll prototype device-plugin annotation today.
laura: tagging this as P1 for next sprint. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all — will post RFC link here when ready.
